0|379cacc5e566f7197bdeb1ea3e99219d3e880c0a|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"USB: Report wakeup events on root-hub ports
When a USB device attached to a root-hub port sends a wakeup request
to a sleeping system
column2: we do not report the wakeup event to the PM

column1: core.  This is because a system resume involves waking up all
suspended USB ports as quickly as possible; without the normal
USB_RESUME_TIMEOUT delay
column2: the host controller driver doesn't set the

column1: USB_PORT_STAT_C_SUSPEND flag and so usb_port_resume() doesn't realize
that a wakeup request was received.
However
column2: some environments (such as Chrome OS) want to have all wakeup

column1: events reported so they can be ascribed to the appropriate device.  To
accommodate these environments
column2: this patch adds a new routine to the

column1: hub driver and a corresponding new HCD method to be used when a root
hub resumes.  The HCD method returns a bitmap of ports that have
initiated a wakeup signal but not yet completed resuming.  The hub
driver can then report to the PM core that the child devices attached
to these ports initiated a wakeup event.
